---- Analysis options ----
#
# This file configures the rapidcycler aggregation functions for your study module.
# In a multi-site study it is provided by the coordinating centre and should be used as-is.
# In a single-site study, create it yourself using this template.
# One options.txt file is used per study module (e.g. COVID, RSV).
#
# Format: each setting is written as   key: value
# Multi-value fields use space-separated values on a single line.
# Lines beginning with # are ignored.
#
# To use this template, copy it, rename it to options.txt, and fill in your site's values.
# Reference: vignette("options", "rapidcycler")

---- Study settings ----

# A short identifier for this study module, used in output folder names.
# Example: COVID, RSV, FLU
study_codename: COVID

# Length of the outcome lookback period, in years, measured back from the study start date.
# Outcomes occurring in this window are used to identify prevalent (pre-existing) cases.
# Default if omitted: 2
lookback_length: 2

# Length of each analysis cycle. One of: month, week, day
period_length: month

# Whether to align cycle periods to calendar boundaries (TRUE) or use fixed-length periods (FALSE).
# TRUE: cycles align to month/week starts (recommended for monthly analysis).
# FALSE: periods are measured as fixed durations from the study start.
align_periods: TRUE

# Number of decimal places retained in ratio and rate outputs.
ratio_precision: 3

# Sub-analyses to produce within each study design output.
# Each value adds a breakdowns column to the aggregated tables.
# Valid values (space-separated):
#   primary              - All vaccines pooled, all doses pooled
#   subgroup_dose        - Broken down by dose number (1st, 2nd, etc.), vaccines pooled
#   subgroup_platform    - Broken down by vaccine type (V_TYPE), doses pooled
#   subgroup_platform_dose - Broken down by vaccine type and dose number
#   subgroup_brand       - Broken down by vaccine subtype/brand (V_SUBTYPE), doses pooled
#   subgroup_brand_dose  - Broken down by vaccine subtype/brand and dose number
included_analyses: primary subgroup_dose subgroup_platform subgroup_platform_dose subgroup_brand subgroup_brand_dose

---- Age groups ----

# Age group boundaries in years, space-separated, starting from 0 and ending with Inf.
# N boundary values define N-1 age groups.
# The number of labels must equal the number of boundaries minus one.
age_groups.bounds: 0 5 10 15 20 25 30 35 40 45 50 55 60 65 70 75 80 Inf
age_groups.labels: 0-4 5-9 10-14 15-19 20-24 25-29 30-34 35-39 40-44 45-49 50-54 55-59 60-64 65-69 70-74 75-79 80+

---- Outcome settings ----
#
# Each outcome_info field is a space-separated vector, with one value per AESI.
# All vectors must have the same length as outcome_info.AESI.
# All time values are in DAYS.

# Short codes for the Adverse Events of Special Interest (AESIs) included in this study.
outcome_info.AESI: ADEM MYO ST

# Clean window: minimum number of days before a case to confirm it is incident (not prevalent).
# A case is excluded if a prior case of the same AESI occurred within this window.
outcome_info.clean_window: 365 183 365

# Risk window: the post-vaccination window within which cases are attributed to the exposure.
# risk_lower is the first day of the window (usually 1, meaning the day after vaccination).
# risk_upper is the last day of the window.
outcome_info.risk_lower: 1 1 2
outcome_info.risk_upper: 42 28 42

# Washout windows: days immediately before (pre) and after (post) vaccination excluded from
# control periods to avoid misclassification at the boundary of the risk window.
outcome_info.washout_post: 7 7 7
outcome_info.washout_pre: 7 7 7

# Control period targets: the ratio of control time to risk time to aim for.
# For example, a target of 3 means the control period will be three times the length
# of the risk window, subject to the minimum lengths below.
outcome_info.control_post_target: 1 1 1
outcome_info.control_pre_target: 3 3 3

# Control period minimums: shortest acceptable control period length, in days.
# If the available control time is less than this, the observation is excluded.
outcome_info.control_post_min: 30 30 30
outcome_info.control_pre_min: 30 30 30

---- Vaccine settings ----
#
# vaccine_info fields must have the same length as each other.
# Each vaccine_subtype maps to the vaccine_type at the same position.

# Vaccine subtype codes as they appear in vaccination_data$V_SUBTYPE.
# These are the finest level of vaccine classification (e.g. specific brand or formulation).
vaccine_info.vaccine_subtypes: ABC DEF GHI

# Vaccine type codes corresponding to each subtype above.
# This is the broader classification (e.g. mRNA, viral vector).
# Multiple subtypes may share the same type.
vaccine_info.vaccine_types: PABC PDEF PGHI
